why: Counting sort when values are small, with a twist: ratings can be huge, but any rating >= n behaves like n for this question, so cap each rating at n, bucket-count them, and scan k from n downward with a running count of ratings >= k.
hints: Sorting descending and finding the last position i with sorted[i] >= i+1 works in O(n log n). Can you avoid the sort?
The answer is at most n, so a rating of 10^9 is no more useful than a rating of n. Cap ratings at n and count them in buckets 0..n.
Walk k from n down to 1, adding bucket[k] to a running total of ratings >= k; return the first k with total >= k, else 0. O(n).
pitfalls: The answer can never exceed n.
This is the h-index problem in disguise.
